title: Gulet Packing List & Onboard Etiquette for a Turkish Blue Cruise
seoTitle: Gulet Packing List Turkey: Onboard Etiquette & Charter Tips
metaDescription: What to pack for a Turkish Blue Cruise gulet: soft bags, deck shoes, AC hours, crew tipping, provisioning, and seasickness tips.
quickAnswer: Pack for a Turkish Blue Cruise in collapsible soft duffle bags with breathable linen, reef-safe sunscreen, and a light windbreaker for evening anchorages. Most gulets enforce a barefoot teak-deck rule, run air-conditioning on generator schedules, and expect 10%–15% crew gratuities in cash alongside pre-agreed provisioning and drinks plans confirmed before embarkation.

body.text: Why should you pack soft duffle bags instead of hard-shell suitcases on a gulet?

Traditional wooden [Turkish gulets](https://goturkiye.com/bluevoyage/turkish-gulets) have compact cabin wardrobes and under-berth lockers built around curved hull lines, leaving almost no flat floor space for rigid luggage. Collapsible soft duffle bags fold flat once unpacked and stow cleanly out of sight, whereas hard-shell suitcases block narrow walkways and scratch varnished mahogany woodwork during coastal swells.

If your Turkish itinerary continues to Istanbul or Cappadocia after sailing, arrange hotel luggage storage or private transfer storage on shore before boarding in Bodrum, Marmaris, Göcek, or Fethiye. Keep one compact dry bag for dinghy landings to Lycian ruins and village piers.

items: Collapsible 50–65L soft duffle bag plus a small 10L waterproof dry bag for tender rides.
Three swimsuits, two quick-dry Turkish cotton peshtemals, and a UV rash guard for midday snorkelling.
Lightweight linen shirts, shorts, and a light windproof jacket for breezy May, June, or October evenings.
Non-marking white-soled boat shoes (optional) and sturdy sandals with ankle straps for rocky shore paths.
Polarised sunglasses with a floating strap, wide-brimmed hat with chin cord, and reef-safe SPF 50 sunscreen.
Motion-sickness remedies, personal prescription medications, and a Type C/F European power adapter.

body.text: How do deck-shoe rules, air-conditioning hours and crew tipping work?

Most gulet captains enforce a strict barefoot policy on teak decks to protect the wood and prevent slips; outside shoes are stored in a basket at boarding. Air-conditioning typically runs 4–8 hours daily on standard charters (up to 24 hours on luxury gulets), and standard crew tips run 10%–15% of the charter fee in cash.

As outlined in local [Göcek Blue Cruise crew etiquette guidelines](https://www.gocekonline.com/en/blue-cruise-guide/plan-your-trip/blue-cruise-crew-etiquette-tipping), treat the captain as your single point of contact for route adjustments, meal timing, or cabin requests. Never enter the galley or crew quarters uninvited, and rinse saltwater off before stepping into the interior saloon.

body.text: What provisioning and drinks plan should you confirm before boarding?

Confirm your exact food and beverage structure at least 14 days before embarkation so the cook can source fresh Aegean produce and seafood. Charters operate on either a fixed per-person daily full-board menu or an APA (Advance Provisioning Allowance, usually 20%–30% of the charter rate) reconciled against supermarket receipts at disembarkation.

Clarify alcohol rules in writing before signing. Some gulets allow guests to bring duty-free wine and spirits on board with zero corkage, while others require all drinks to be purchased from the yacht bar list. Send dietary restrictions, allergies, and children's preferences on a written preference sheet well ahead of departure along Türkiye's [Blue Voyage coastline](https://goturkiye.com/culturaljourneys/blue-voyage).
How do you handle seasickness on calm vs open stretches?

Protected gulfs like Göcek and Hisarönü stay remarkably flat in summer, so most guests feel little motion while anchored or motoring inside sheltered bays. Open-water crossings—such as rounding Cape Knidos or crossing between Kekova and Kaş during afternoon Meltemi winds—produce short chop where preventative medication, deck-level horizon focus, and early morning departures make all the difference.

Take non-drowsy motion-sickness tablets 60 minutes before leaving calm anchorage if wind forecasts exceed 15 knots. Stay midships in fresh air rather than reading below deck, sip ginger tea or still water, and ask your captain to schedule exposed headlands early in the morning before thermal breezes build.

faq.q: Can I bring a small carry-on roller bag on a Turkish gulet?
faq.a: Only if your captain confirms spare locker space in advance. Even compact hard-shell cabin rollers are awkward to store in wooden cabins; transferring belongings into a collapsible duffle bag before boarding is strongly recommended.

faq.q: Are beach towels and bath towels provided on board?
faq.a: Yes. Almost all crewed Turkish gulets supply bath towels and deck towels, changed mid-week. Packing one lightweight Turkish peshtemal is still useful for shore excursions and quick drying after swims.

faq.q: How is the crew tip distributed at the end of a Blue Cruise?
faq.a: Guests place the cash gratuity (typically Euros or US Dollars) in a sealed envelope and hand it to the captain on the final morning. The captain divides it fairly among the cook, deckhands, and stewardess.

faq.q: Can we sleep on deck under the stars during summer?
faq.a: Yes. Sleeping on the cushioned aft lounge or sun mattresses is a classic Blue Cruise tradition from June through September. Bring a light long-sleeve layer for pre-dawn dew and check with the crew about mosquito screens when anchored near pine marshes.

faq.q: Do gulets have Wi-Fi and mobile signal along the coast?
faq.a: Most private gulets provide a 4G/5G router with a monthly data cap. Signal is reliable near Bodrum, Göcek, Fethiye, and Kaş, though remote coves between Marmaris and Datça experience brief dead zones.

faq.q: What happens if bad weather prevents sailing to a planned bay?
faq.a: Maritime safety always rests with the captain. If high winds or swell make an exposed bay unsafe, the captain will pivot to a sheltered cove along the coast without compromising swimming or shore-dining stops.
